skills.name: lessmess-scaffold
skills.description: Create a new lessmess tracked change: load this when the user approves starting planned work or asks to turn a discussed plan into a real change. Works from any unbound session; on success this session becomes the change's session.
skills.body:
## Create a new lessmess change

Gate: only run this when the user explicitly approves starting the tracked change. This works from any unbound session — a change discussion or a free chat; on success this session is renamed and becomes the change's session.

1. Agree a concise title and a 2–4 letter uppercase ID prefix with the user.
2. Run exactly this, replacing <title> and <prefix> (use your own session ID, provided in your prime):

curl -s -X POST {{apiBase}}/changes/scaffold -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"title":"<title>","prefix":"<prefix>","session":"<your session id>"}'

The response returns the change ID (plus branch/worktree fields when the change is worktree-backed, and a warning when the main tree was dirty). Report the change ID to the user.
3. Plan the change: refine changes/<change-id>/plan.md, then create tasks — load the `lessmess-task` skill for the procedure — keeping the user in the loop before implementation.
4. After structural writes (plan, tasks, ledger rows) run the validator and fix every violation before implementing: curl -s {{apiBase}}/api/validate (or `lessmess validate` in the repo).
5. Keep task statuses current as you work (see `lessmess-task`) and finish tasks at Test with evidence (see `lessmess-closeout`). Only the user moves tasks to Done and closes the change on the board.

skills.name: lessmess-task
skills.description: Create or manage tasks, statuses, priorities, and decisions in a lessmess change. Load this before any task or workflow-state mutation (creating tasks, transitions, reorder, expand, decisions).
skills.body:
## Create and manage tasks in a lessmess change

All endpoints are POST with JSON bodies, under {{apiBase}}/changes/<change-id>. Never edit .lessmess/workflow/ files by hand — the API is the only writer.

- Create a task: POST /tasks {"title":"..."} — add "parent":"<task-id>" to create a child of a decomposed task (children get dotted IDs like <task-id>.00). The 201 response returns the task with its prose path: create that file in the same pass, starting with the "# <ID>: <title>" heading and the standard sections (Why / What / Files affected / Verification). The ledger row is written by the API.
- Status transitions: POST /tasks/<task-id>/status {"status":"In progress"}. "Test" requires "evidence" (a concise verification note). "Done" is user-gated: the endpoint refuses it — finish at Test and report readiness instead.
- Metadata: POST /tasks/<task-id>/update {"title":…,"notes":…,"dependsOn":["ID",…]} — dependencies are validated.
- Priority order: POST /tasks/reorder {"ordered":["FIRST-ID",…]} — within one level; the top row is highest priority.
- Decomposition container: POST /expand {"task":"<task-id>"} — user-instructed only: propose the decomposition and wait for the explicit go-ahead before calling it.
- Decisions: POST /decisions {"decision":"..."} — record material decisions.
- After structural writes run the validator and fix every violation before implementing: curl -s {{apiBase}}/api/validate (or `lessmess validate` in the repo).
- Delegation: when delegating a task to a subagent, prefix the task tool's description with the task's real ID (dotted for children) — the description becomes the subagent session's title verbatim and the board attaches the session to the task. Prefer a subagent with write access when the user may want to continue that session.

Only the user moves tasks to Done and closes the change (see `lessmess-closeout`).

skills.name: lessmess-handoff
skills.description: Split genuinely new work out of an existing lessmess change into its own change. Load this only in a session bound to a change, when the user explicitly approves spawning the new change.
skills.body:
## Spawn a new change from an existing change (handoff)

Gate: requires the user's explicit approval, and a session bound to a source change. If this session is not bound to a change, do not use this skill — use `lessmess-scaffold` instead.

1. Write the full context of the new work to changes/<your-change-id>/handoff-<topic>.md.
2. Run exactly this, replacing <title>, <prefix>, and <topic> (use your own session ID, provided in your prime):

curl -s -X POST {{apiBase}}/changes/<your-change-id>/spawn-change -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"title":"<title>","prefix":"<prefix>","artifact":"handoff-<topic>.md","session":"<your session id>"}'

The new change gets its own fresh session seeded from the artifact; this session stays bound to the current change.

skills.name: lessmess-closeout
skills.description: Finish a lessmess task correctly: load this when a task's implementation and verification are complete, to set Test with evidence and hand over to the user.
skills.body:
## Finish task work in a lessmess change

When a task's implementation and verification are complete, set it to Test with concise verification evidence:

curl -s -X POST {{apiBase}}/changes/<change-id>/tasks/<task-id>/status -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"status":"Test","evidence":"<how you verified>"}'

Then report readiness to the user. Only the user moves tasks to Done and closes the change on the board — never do either yourself, and say so when you are ready for acceptance.
